title: Lords of Montpellier
summary: This document covers the Lordship of Montpellier, a feudal jurisdiction in Languedoc centered on the city of Montpellier that existed from 986 to 1344. The document begins with the formation of the lordship, describing how Ricuin II, bishop of Mauguio, granted the lands in fief to the knight Guiu I, whose successors (beginning with William I) expanded the territory. It notes that Montpellier was a relatively young city compared to Roman-era neighbors like Nîmes and Narbonne, but developed rapidly into a significant economic and cultural trading hub linking northern Europe, Spain, and the Mediterranean, thanks to its strategic location near the Via Domitia and the port of Lattes. The core of the document is a chronological list of the lords of Montpellier, organized by ruling dynasty: the House of Montpellier (986–1204), featuring a succession of rulers named William ending with Maria of Montpellier; the House of Aragon (1213–1344), beginning with James I and including the kings of Majorca; and finally the French royal domain, detailing how James III sold the lordship to King Philip VI of France in 1344, and how it was later ceded to Charles II of Navarre in 1364 as part of a peace treaty following the Battle of Cocherel. The document concludes with references and sources, including Archibald Lewis's 1971 study, "The Guillems of Montpellier: A Sociological Appraisal."
